packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Transcribe what you can see, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Only one cropped image is supplied. I count six physical lines from the top. The sixth line is cut through by the bottom edge. The right edge also appears to interrupt text. There is one visible text block; no separate marginal addition or second column can be established. The lettering is faded and several readings below are very uncertain. These are visual readings, not a reconstructed continuous Latin text.

image-001.png:1  Ex? [illegible] ita? [illegible] eadē? [illegible]
image-001.png:2  hoc? i? recto? quali[illegible] autē? [illegible] a corpore?
image-001.png:3  [illegible] que? [illegible] popule? [illegible]
image-001.png:4  animalis? [illegible] [illegible] et? alio? e[illegible]
image-001.png:5  Qui? pr̄? [illegible] [illegible] [illegible] et?
image-001.png:6  [illegible]

Abbreviations and uncertainty
The macrons in eadē? and autē? represent apparent marks above the final portion of the word; both the base reading and the identification of the marks are uncertain. If those base readings are correct, possible expansions are eadē? (eadem?) and autē? (autem?). In line 5, pr̄? is an uncertain initial reading with an apparent abbreviation mark; I cannot justify an expansion. Other small supralinear traces cannot reliably be distinguished from faint strokes, surface marks, or show-through. I have not expanded them.

Corrections and additions
No deletion, replacement, or inserted word can be identified confidently in this crop. This does not establish that there are none. There are no separately legible marginal additions.

Limitations
The result is deliberately fragmentary. Even some words marked with question marks may be wrong. The faint, compressed script makes segmentation uncertain, so the [illegible] spans do not indicate a count of missing words. Line 6 preserves only upper portions of letters and is not transcribed speculatively. I have not supplied words by grammatical inference. No overlap assessment is possible with a single image.
